## Summary

**The Problem**: The screenshot compression system was configured to compress **every** screenshot immediately to text summaries, which meant the AI agent never got to see actual screenshots. This completely broke computer use functionality since the agent needs to see actual images to understand what's on screen and where to interact.

**The Root Cause**: 
- `immediate_compression: true` by default
- `max_base64_screenshots: 1` by default  
- `enable_screenshot_compression: true` by default

This meant every screenshot was converted to text like "Screenshot captured at timestamp with moderate complexity..." instead of sending the actual image.

**The Fix**:

1. **Updated Constants** (`src-tauri/src/constants/memory.rs`):
   - Changed `DEFAULT_MAX_BASE64_SCREENSHOTS` from `1` to `8` 
   - Set `immediate_compression` to `false` in the default config
   - Added clear comments explaining these are for computer use

2. **Updated Memory Manager** (`src-tauri/src/agent/implementations/memory_manager.rs`):
   - Modified `VisualContextConfig::default()` to use the corrected constants
   - Ensured computer use agents can see up to 8 actual screenshots

3. **Regenerated TypeScript Constants**:
   - Confirmed `VISUAL_DEFAULT_MAX_BASE64_SCREENSHOTS: 8` in the generated constants

**The Result**: 
- Computer use agents will now see actual screenshots (up to 8 at a time)
- Screenshots will only be compressed when memory pressure is high or when they're old
- This maintains the token optimization benefits while preserving computer use functionality

The fix has been tested with a successful compilation check. Your computer use agent should now be able to see actual screenshots instead of text summaries!
